question: Two circles touch each other externally at C. AB is a direct common tangent to the two circles, A and B are points of contact and ∠CAB = 55°. Then ∠ACB is:
solution:
**Given:**

AB is a direct common tangent

∠CAB = 55°

**Concept used:**

Tangents drawn from a external point on the circle will be equal in length and

their corresponding angle will also be equal

Sum of angles in triangle will be 180°

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/12a55d33328c5ac3ae1284c87273914ec7df2b90be972ed298a53a8de1a8eb84.png] 

Draw a line from Point C to Point D lies on tangent AB

⇒ AD = CD (tangents from external point D)

⇒ ∠CAD = ∠ACD = 55°

⇒ Similarly DB = CD (tangents from external point D)

⇒ ∠DCB = ∠DBC = x° (Let)

Now,

In triangle ABC

⇒ ∠CAD + ∠ACD + ∠DCB + ∠DBC = 180°

⇒ 55° + 55° + x° + x° = 180°

⇒ 2x° = 70°

⇒ x° = 35°

⇒ ∠ACB = ∠ACD + ∠DCB = 55° + 35° = 90°

**∴ The correct answer is 90°.**
